body.title: Lyrics in the background hinder reading for listeners and nearby classmates
body.abstract: Students often study with music in shared spaces such as libraries and dorm rooms. In two experiments in a simulated study hall, participants who listened to music with lyrics while reading scored lower on a comprehension test than participants who read in silence, and participants seated next to a listener whose music was audible scored lower than those seated next to a quiet peer. Instrumental music had smaller effects. The results suggest that music with lyrics is a distraction for listeners and for the people around them.
